subject: Production latency & 5xx on reserved pool — urgent remediation needed
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@primelane.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@primelane.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency & 5xx — seeing sustained impact

Vanessa,

We're seeing a sustained production degradation starting early this morning (UTC). Our SREs report: p99 latency jumped from ~150ms to ~2.4s, error rate is ~6% (5xx) for inference endpoints backed by our reserved capacity, and token queueing is building in the client. The incident is causing downstream timeouts and customer-facing errors.

This is live: we have customers degrading sessions and one large merchant is threatening to pause traffic. Our monitoring shows reserved throughput is fully consumed and requests are being rate-limited despite our contract. We opened a support ticket (https://hubspot.company/contacts/primelane/7842) but need immediate triage and a bridge.

Can Redwood confirm root cause and provide an ETA for relief? We need a fix or a temporary mitigation (fallback routing, burst allocation, credits) ASAP.

Alex Park
CTO, PrimeLane
alex.park@primelane.com
[Attachment: primelane_sla_screenshot.png (image/png)]
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@primelane.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx — seeing sustained impact

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. Sorry you're seeing this. I'm pulling David (Customer Ops) and Marissa (SE) onto this now.

Immediate plan:
- We will stand up a 30-minute bridge to triage. Suggested times: 09:35 or 09:45 PST. Please confirm what works for your SREs.
- David will run a targeted diagnostic against your reserved pool and token queueing.
- Short-term mitigation options: route a percentage of traffic to a compatible hosted model variant (will need your sign-off), enable a temporary burst allocation from our shared pool, or apply a routing throttle to prevent downstream client timeouts while we remediate.

I will keep you updated in-line. We're treating this as high priority.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alex Park <alex.park@primelane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx — preliminary findings and mitigation

Alex / Vanessa — joined the bridge and pulled initial telemetry. Summary of what we see:

- Root cause signal: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 backing PrimeLane's reservation is experiencing sustained oversubscription driven by a combination of a noisy-tenant spike and a model execution regression after a recent quantization change on our side. Kernel selection degraded for certain sequence-length patterns and a subset of nodes fell behind, which cascaded into increased KV cache misses and longer per-token execution.
- Customer-facing impact: reserved throughput limit reached -> automatic rate-limiting engaged for your reservation; request queueing increased leading to p99 spikes and 5xx retries.

Immediate actions taken (in-flight):
1) Throttled low-priority background traffic and temporarily disabled non-critical batch jobs in the same cluster.
2) Pushed an emergency routing rule to shift 20% of weighted production traffic to a hosted compatible variant (same model family, slightly different quantization profile) to reduce pressure on the dedicated pool.
3) Requested 8 burst GPU nodes in us-west-2 from the provisioning pool (pending auto-approval). If approved, we expect partial relief within 18–30 minutes.
4) Captured ops snapshot (ops_snapshot_20261120.tar.gz) and created OPS-9123 in Jira for a follow-up RCA.

Estimated timeline: partial traffic relief 20–30 minutes after burst allocation; full remediation (kernel fixes + rebalancing) expected within ~4 hours.

Customer concessions proposed: immediate one-time burst credit (internal approval required) and a goodwill billing credit of 5% for the impacted invoice period.

I'll continue to post updates here.

-David
David Kim
Director, Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
[Attachment: ops_snapshot_20261120.tar.gz (application/gzip)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec note — request for emergency burst & credit authorization

Team — quick summary for execs and finance: PrimeLane (DL-78321) is experiencing dedicated-pool saturation in us-west-2 causing p99 latency >2s and visible 5xx. David's mitigation is active (20% traffic shift + burst request). We need fast approval for:

- Emergency burst allocation (8 GPU nodes in us-west-2) — estimated cost impact up to $28k for the day.
- One-time goodwill credit up to 5% of November invoice or up to $50k (whichever is lower) to preserve the relationship.

Rationale: PrimeLane is a priority enterprise account (on reserved capacity), churn risk is material given merchant outages, and the short-term cost is justified to avoid contract-level SLA breaches.

Please reply with approvals (EMERGENCY-BURST / GOODWILL-CREDIT) or escalate if you want a narrower concession. I will trigger procurement if we have two approvers.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Product & Ops — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Quick update: burst nodes auto-approved at 10:02 PST and partial relief observed by 10:22 PST (p99 dropped to ~550ms). PrimeLane SREs are validating session stability. David is tracking the RCA for a permanent kernel fix.

Alex — we will follow up with a formal incident summary and proposed credit. Thank you for patience — will keep you posted on the RCA timeline.

Vanessa Ortiz
